items.q: In the Cockcroft & Gault numerator, the patient's age is subtracted from:
items.exp: Creatinine clearance = (140 − age) × body weight ÷ (72 × S.creatinine) in males. (Book p735)

items.q: Fill up: The book labels the Cockcroft & Gault equation as a ______ formula, which explains why it is still used despite being obsolete.
items.exp: Two lines appear under the formula: 'Bed side formula' and 'Not preferred now d/t disadvantages'. (Book p735)

items.q: MDRD, as the page expands the abbreviation, is the society for:
opts: Measurement of drug dosing in renal disease
Mapping of dysfunction in renal dialysis
items.exp: Entry 2 reads: MDRD equation — by society for modification of diet & renal diseases. (Book p735)

items.q: The stated advantage of the CKD-EPI equation appears once the GFR is above:

Match each equation with the label attached to it on this page — 1) Cockcroft & Gault 2) MDRD and CKD-EPI 3) CKD-EPI alone … A) Best when GFR is above 60 B) Obsolete, bed side formula C) Preferred now D) Used to estimate GFR in children
items.exp: Cockcroft & Gault = obsolete bed side formula; MDRD and CKD-EPI are bracketed as 'Preferred now'; CKD-EPI alone carries 'Best (Advantage when GFR > 60)'. Schwartz is the children's equation. (Book p735)

items.q: According to the table, the Cockcroft & Gault equation overestimates GFR because creatinine is filtered and also secreted.
opts: True — clearance equals GFR plus tubular secretion
False — the page says it underestimates GFR for the same reason
True — because alkaline picrate assays under-read creatinine
False — tubular secretion only affects IDMs-based assays
items.exp: The disadvantage column lists 'Cr is secreted → CrCl = GFR + Tubular secretion', alongside clearance = GFR + secretion or GFR − absorption, which is why the estimate over-reads true GFR. (Book p735)
